newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mixed, investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mixed, investors sidelined.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed mixed on Tuesday as the yen's gains against the dollar offset a firmer Chicago market overnight, traders said.
Prices ranged from 10 yen lower to 180 yen higher, with the benchmark January 1998 contract up 80 yen at 14,350 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 39,473 lots.

Local investors were largely sidelined today, as the yen's rise against the dollar offset Chicago's price gains, traders said. "Technical trading dominated the market. Many investors will be reluctant to trade until the announcement of the USDA's crop report later this week," a trader said.
As of 0815 GMT, the spot March corn contract on the CBOT Project A system was last traded at $2.58 per bushel, up from $2.57 at Monday's Chicago close.
Spot January CBOT soybean futures on Project A were at $6.94-1/2, up from $6.94.
